transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood CSM), Alyssa (BlueHarbor Lead Eng), Marcus (BlueHarbor CTO), Danielle (PM)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in to review integration progress. Demo of SDK tool/function calls for payment normalization, review of structured output schema, and discussion of early perf numbers from staging. Action items assigned for benchmarks, security docs, and SDK snippets.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, good to see you. Quick roll call? 
[00:05] Alyssa: Alyssa here. 
[00:06] Marcus: Marcus here. 
[00:08] Danielle: Danielle, on the PM side. 
[00:09] Samir: Great. Lena and Marta with us from Redwood? 
[00:11] Lena: Yep Lena, SE. 
[00:12] Marta: Marta, CSM. 
[00:15] Samir: Cool. Agenda: quick integration notes, Lena will show the SDK + function/tool calls and structured output for transaction normalization, then we review the perf numbers you ran last week, and finish with next steps. Anything to add? 
[00:26] Danielle: No that covers it. We're keen on the structured output bit, want to see examples. 
[00:31] Samir: Perfect, Lena take it away. 
[00:33] Lena: OK, so we pushed the SDK snippet to the repo earlier this morning. We're using the JS SDK but same pattern in Python. High level: you create a client with your key, then register a function schema for payment_normalize and a tool connector for your internal ledger service. The SDK supports both "tool calls" and "function calls" — tools for external HTTP/webhook integrations, functions for deterministic typed responses. 
[00:54] [00:55] Alyssa: Quick question, is the function call synchronous? We need determinism for the downstream job. 
[00:59] Lena: Function calls return typed JSON synchronously in the response payload; tool calls are proxied and can be async via callbacks if you set up webhooks. For your use case, payment normalization, function calls are a good fit because you want a fixed schema back. 
[01:17] Marcus: Are there size limits for the response? Some of our transactions have long memo fields. 
[01:22] Lena: We recommend truncating memos on the agent side and storing metadata in your ledger. The runtime has configurable output length, but for structured output we enforce schema which helps keep things tight. 
[01:34] [01:35] Danielle: Can you show the structured output example? 
[01:36] Lena: Sure. Example: {"tx_id": "string", "amount_cents": "int", "currency": "string", "normalized_payee": "string", "category": "enum: [transfer,payment,fee]", "confidence": "float"} — we then validate via the SDK helper and emit both the typed json and a human_readable summary. 
[02:00] Alyssa: I noticed in the example we got last week the normalized_payee sometimes split names oddly — like "ACME Inc" into two tokens. Is that model tuning or prompt? 
[02:10] Lena: Could be both. We saw that too; tuning the prompt with more examples and using a small rule-based post-processing step reduced errors. Also switching to a higher-accuracy variant during post-processing helps. 
[02:25] Samir: That's a good segway to perf: Marta, can you confirm what we saw for latency on staging? 
[02:30] Marta: Yep, from the test harness BlueHarbor shared — their default hosted run on Redwood dev region avg p95 around 220ms per token? Sorry per request, for structured function calls it averaged 380ms latency median and p95 780ms. This was with the shared host pool and batching disabled since you were testing near-real-time. 
[02:55] Marcus: 780ms p95 seems high for our SLA, we were hoping for <300ms p95. 
[03:02] Lena: The big lever is dedicated vs hosted and quantization profile. With Dedicated reserved GPU pool and config for continuous KV cache we expect p95 <300ms for your typical 256 token context. Also we can tune batching threshold for low-latency profiles and enable prefix caching for recurring prompts. 
[03:23] Alyssa: Can you quantify cost difference? Running dedicated is a big jump for us. 
[03:28] Samir: Right — we estimated in our last deck roughly 3x unit cost for dedicated at your current volume, but that's rough. Redwood Optimize can run a workload analysis to recommend batching/quantization to cut cost by up to 40% while keeping p95 under target. We'll run a targeted estimate. 
[03:46] [03:47] Danielle: About auth — we need SSO + SAML and KMS integration. Where are we on that? 
[03:53] Marta: We have a PKG for SSO and SAML, and KMS integrations are supported. I'll share the network diagram and KMS notes after the call. You'll be able to bring your own KMS in Private and keys for Dedicated as well. 
[04:07] Marcus: For audit logs, can we get token-level traceability for each request? 
[04:12] Lena: Yes, Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns and full audit traces. We can map request ids back to your internal ids if you pass correlation_id in the SDK header. 
[04:25] Alyssa: Great. Back to the SDK: in our PoC we tried a hybrid approach: call a tool to fetch ledger metadata then function to normalize. But the test shows extra round-trips. Any pattern to reduce that? 
[04:36] Lena: Two patterns: 1) pre-fetch and cache frequently-needed ledger lookups via a synchronous tool with caching TTLs, or 2) use a single function schema that accepts raw payload plus optional ledger snapshot as field. The latter increases token size but avoids the extra network hop. For BlueHarbor we recommended using pre-populated KV cache for the most common payees and falling back to tool calls. 
[05:02] Alyssa: Ok we'll try pre-populated KV cache. How do we seed it? 
[05:06] Lena: You can upload a CSV via the Console or call the runtime API to seed KV entries; we'll send the snippet. 
[05:12] [05:13] Samir: Let's review the actual test results you sent. Alyssa, you uploaded the harness results on Monday? 
[05:20] Alyssa: Yes, we ran three profiles: 1) Hosted baseline (no batching), 2) Hosted with lightweight batching (50ms window), 3) Dedicated small pool. I can summarize if useful. 
[05:30] Marta: We have the numbers in the shared sheet. Quick headline: Hosted baseline med 410ms, p95 920ms; batching host med 360ms, p95 650ms; Dedicated med 210ms, p95 290ms. 
[05:48] Marcus: That dedicated p95 290ms is closer to our target but cost was about 2.9x of hosted per token. 
[05:55] Samir: Right. So decision levers: accept higher cost for lower latency, or optimize via caching/batching/quantization and stay hosted. We recommended a mixed routing policy — low-latency critical paths to Dedicated, background processing on hosted. 
[06:13] Danielle: For our use case, payments that trigger customer-facing flows need <300ms p95. Others can be async. So mixed routing makes sense. 
[06:22] [06:23] Alyssa: On the structured output validation we had a couple of schema mismatches — some fields were null or typed as string instead of int. Is there a schema validator we can plug into our pipeline? 
[06:34] Lena: Yes, the SDK includes a validation helper that will coerce types where safe and surface validation errors. You can configure it to reject the response or fall back to a human review path. We'll include that snippet in the SDK update. 
[06:48] Samir: Also, note that function schemas support enums and required fields; making tx_id required reduced downstream errors in other customers. 
[06:55] Marcus: Any recommendations for regression testing? We have a suite of 500 canonical prompts. 
[07:00] Lena: Great, bring those into our Eval harness. We can run A/B between model variants and track metric regressions on normalized fields. You can schedule daily runs against a staging snapshot. 
[07:12] Alyssa: We tried the Eval harness but had trouble with auth tokens. 
[07:17] Marta: I'll coordinate with you after the call to get service account creds for the eval runs. 
[07:22] [07:23] Danielle: On the SDK examples, can you include a sample flow that does: 1) tool call to ledger if cache miss, 2) function call to normalize, 3) structured output validation, 4) emit event to our webhook? 
[07:36] Lena: Yep that's the exact pattern in the updated repo. We'll add extra comments for your pattern. 
[07:41] Alyssa: One more question about error handling: if the function returns a validation error, how do we surface that without blocking? 
[07:47] Lena: We recommend returning a 200 with a status object in the structured output that flags validation_error and includes suggested fallback instructions; then your ingestion can push to a human-review queue. 
[07:59] Marcus: Sounds good. Any security risks if we send raw ledger ids to the runtime? 
[08:05] Marta: Sensitive fields can be redacted on ingest or encrypted via client-side KMS. For Private deployments we support stricter data residency. We'll include the network diagram. 
[08:18] Samir: Alright, I want to cover a small demo — Lena, can you run the SDK sample and show the function call flow? 
[08:24] Lena: Sure, screen-share — running the JS sample now. 
[08:30] [08:31] Lena: Initiating function call: payload with tx, amount, memo. Response: returns typed json with tx_id, amount_cents 12500, currency USD, normalized_payee "Blue Harbor Utilities", category "payment", confidence 0.97. Human summary: "Payment to Blue Harbor Utilities $125.00". 
[08:54] Alyssa: That normalized_payee looks better. Did you change the prompt? 
[08:58] Lena: Yes, added two-shot examples and forced stricter delimiter guidance; also increased temperature to 0.0 on function calls. 
[09:07] Danielle: Temperature 0.0 for deterministic output makes sense. 
[09:10] Marcus: Any plan for canarying model rollouts? We want to be cautious. 
[09:15] Samir: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts by percent of traffic and automatic rollback on regression metrics. We'll help you set alerts on the normalized_payee accuracy and latency. 
[09:26] [09:27] Alyssa: Good. Back to performance — do you have recommended quantization profiles for Dedicated? Our infra team worries about model quality regression. 
[09:35] Lena: For the models you tested, 8-bit quantization with per-channel mapping preserved accuracy in our tests; 4-bit aggressive knobs introduce small regressions. We'll run an eval on your 500 canonical prompts to measure accuracy delta; that will inform profile recommendation. 
[09:52] Samir: Quick check — timeline: you expect to finish eval and decide by mid-April? Danielle? 
[09:58] Danielle: Yes our target for a pilot decision is April 15. We want numbers and a small pilot ready by then. 
[10:05] Marta: Noted. We'll prioritize the benchmark and the SDK updates. 
[10:09] [10:10] Samir: Any blockers we should know about? 
[10:12] Alyssa: Just the eval harness creds and the KV seed upload API snippet. Also need the security docs. 
[10:18] Marta: We'll send all three items this week. 
[10:21] Samir: OK let's do a quick recap of next steps. 
[10:23] Lena: I'll run the dedicated benchmark and share config + results (due 2026-04-07). 
[10:28] Samir: I'll update the SDK repo with BlueHarbor-specific examples and tool/function patterns (due 2026-04-02). 
[10:33] Marta: I'll email the SOC2/ISO pack, network diagram, and KMS integration notes (due 2026-04-03). 
[10:39] Alyssa: We'll provide the 500 canonical prompts and the throughput expectations (due 2026-04-06). 
[10:44] Marcus: Thanks all. 
[10:46] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the CRM and Slack. Meet again same time next week? 
[10:51] Danielle: Works for us. 
[10:52] Samir: OK closing.

End of transcript.
